scenes.headline: How a trillion-parameter model is built and served
scenes.sub: MiMo-V2.6: four-bit weights, a thirty-step RL run, a block drafter.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Daisy! MiMo-V2.6 Pro is a trillion-parameter open model. Here's how it's stored, trained and sped up.

scenes.label: The idea
scenes.text: A trillion parameters shipped natively in four bits, tuned by just thirty RL steps, and served with a drafter that fills eight slots at once.
scenes.say: A trillion parameters in four bits, tuned by thirty RL steps, served with a drafter that fills eight slots at once.

steps.say: Pro has seventy layers. Sixty see only a hundred and twenty-eight token window; ten are global, buying back the reach.
Each feed-forward holds three hundred and eighty-four experts, top eight, none shared. About forty-two billion parameters work per token.

steps.note: MXFP4: 566 GB, not about 2 TB in BF16
steps.say: And the release is the four-bit checkpoint: five hundred and sixty-six gigabytes, not about two terabytes.
The model card draws it: sliding-window blocks, then one global block, each with a sparse mixture of experts.
Image and audio encoders feed their tokens in, interleaved.

items.say: The whole RL run is thirty optimizer steps, each on fifteen hundred and sixty-eight prompts, sixteen rollouts apiece.
The router is frozen, so the experts re-tune inside the routing that pre-training learned.
Pass or fail can't rank two passing answers, so passing runs are ranked, and advantage shifts to the better ones.

steps.say: Fill the next eight positions with a mask token. A five-layer drafter reads them in one pass, guided by target hidden states.
It drafts seven tokens, the target checks the block once, and keeps the longest matching prefix. Same quality, by construction.

steps.note: claimed up to 20x; a block of 8 caps it at 8x
steps.say: But a block is eight positions, so one target pass yields at most eight tokens: eight times fewer passes, not the claimed twenty.

scenes.text: The lasting part is the RL release: about 7,000 graded environments with their verifiers, and a baseline with denominators printed.
scenes.say: What will last is the RL release: about seven thousand graded environments, each with its verifier.

recap: A trillion parameters, shipped in four bits
Thirty RL steps with the router frozen
scenes.say: To recap: four-bit weights, thirty RL steps, and a drafter capped at eight.
